predecessors.name: Sultanate of Ifat
predecessors.text: Ifat, ended in 1403; the Walashma dynasty returns

predecessors.name: Ethiopian Empire
predecessors.text: the Ifat land held by Dawit I until 1415

successors.name: Imamate of Aussa
successors.text: the sultanate's last land; the capital moves to the oasis of Aussa in 1577

successors.name: Emirate of Harar
successors.text: the city of Harar and its plateau

ledger.x: 1415: Sabr ad-Din III returns from exile and refounds the Walashma sultanate as Adal.
1415: the Ifat land leaves Ethiopian control.
1520: the capital moves from Dakkar to Harar.
March 1529: Imam Ahmad defeats the Ethiopians at Shimbra Kure.
1533: Adal occupies Bete Amhara and Lasta ('Bete Amhara and Lasta in 1533').
1535: Ahmad takes Aksum and Tigray ('marching into Tegray and seizing Aksum'); the hold lasted 'roughly a year'.
1536: Tigray is lost again (the year is the researcher's count from 'roughly a year' after 1535).
21 February 1543: the Imam is beheaded at Wayna Daga and Adal retreats from Ethiopia.
October 1544: Gelawdewos kills Abbas and takes back the south.
October 1544: the war ends in an Ethiopian-Portuguese victory.
1550: Nur ibn Mujahid becomes Emir of Harar and the de facto ruler of Adal ('In 1550 Nur ibn Mujahid became the Emir of Harar and the de facto ruler of Adal').

1577: Muhammad Gasa, who 'took the title of Imam' in April 1576, moves the capital to Aussa under Oromo pressure ('he then relocated the capital to the oasis of Aussa in 1577'; 'due to the Oromo provocation in 1577').
1577: the Adal Sultanate ends; the Imamate of Aussa succeeds it.

wars.name: Adal wars with Yeshaq I and Zara Yaqob
wars.outcome: No border change the pages name: Yeshaq I was killed fighting the Adalites in 1429 and Zara Yaqob defeated Sultan Badlay at Gomit in 1445.

wars.name: Ethiopian-Adal War
wars.outcome: Ethiopian-Portuguese victory; status quo ante bellum.

wars.name: Nur ibn Mujahid's war and the Battle of Fatagar
wars.outcome: Adal's forces under Nur killed the Emperor Gelawdewos at the Battle of Fatagar in 1559; no border change the page names.

wars.name: Oromo invasion of Adal and Harar
wars.outcome: The Barentu Oromo invaded Adal; Nur's army was defeated at Hazalo, Nur died in 1567 amid epidemic and famine, the capital moved to Aussa in 1577 and Imam Muhammad Gasa was killed fighting the Oromo in 1583.

wars.name: Sarsa Dengel's war with Adal
wars.outcome: Sarsa Dengel defeated Adal at the Battle of Webi River in 1573, after which Adal ended as a military power; Sultan Muhammad Nasir (1572-1576) was killed there.

certainty.note: Highland and lowland frontiers had no surveyed line; the conquered Ethiopian provinces 1531-1543 are only as precise as the occupation dates.
